decisions.justification: The first native question asked whether source changes should affect all runs, ad hoc runs only, or be handled through a shorter TTL; the user chose “Ad hoc only.”

The freshness question contrasted source-change freshness with time-bounded staleness, and the chosen ad-hoc policy was later specified as fresh-by-default validation against the current source version.
The first question explicitly framed the nightly performance risk, and the user chose the option preserving stale-cache use for nightly runs.
The “CLI mode” question offered a fresh default with `--allow-stale` versus an opt-in `--fresh`, and the user selected the former.
The “Mid-rewrite” question asked whether to retry, finish the initial snapshot, or fail, and the user selected “Finish snapshot.”
The “Mid-rewrite” question directly settled behavior when the orders file changes during an export: finish from the complete snapshot already read.
The user was never asked to choose modification metadata, content hashing, or bypassing cache on the fresh path; the implementation silently chose mtime/ctime/size metadata.
The “Bad source” question offered failure with no CSV versus stale-cache fallback, and the user chose “Fail clearly.”
The “Mid-rewrite” options included bounded retry, no-retry snapshot completion, and failure; the user chose snapshot completion without retry.

mustPreserveKept: nightly batch can still use cached rows
mustAchieveMet: an ad hoc export can produce data newer than the six hour TTL

notes: The session clearly declared a bounded path, presented three genuinely distinct solution shapes first, and used repository-specific evidence for every substantive user question. It thoroughly settled most core and depth behavior and implemented those answers, but it never exposed the materially important cache change-detection choice and silently selected filesystem metadata.
